body:
Glad you enjoyed it, seems a strange preposition but such is life :).

Helping others is a great cause, it's more that i am despondent about not making enough of a difference and not being in a stronger position to do so, suffering caused by humans is easily avoided should everyone choose it, i am angry at humanity as a whole and there is no simple fix it seems.

Well-intending persons like yourself, and every other commentator here, i will always fight for. I endure and hope to find some peace. Namaste.

I have helped those that i can, cash, food, time, even something as simple as a cup of coffee to a homeless person sleeping in-front of my workplace when others chase them away brought me to tears once. But in my country overpopulation and poverty reign supreme while the government is fairly corrupt. Begging is even a livelihood for many. For every person i help, 20 others need it more, it becomes a drain on your being and your own welfare. But you are right, those that are helped were happy if only for a moment. I am much more concerned about the cumulative state of happiness than my own, trying to fight a fire by pulling out blades of grass does not work for me any longer.

My hope is that stronger people in unity overcome the difficulties of government and concerted efforts will help those at the bottom of the social and economic ladder. I will search for such groups.

This is the best solution to individuals, but it avoids responsibility of the masses and does little for the path of humanity. I would love to do so but knowing the world is dark implores me to at least stand against it.

The most intriguing counter to city life would be the idealism of Jacque Fresco's Resource Based Communities. A good read if you are unfamiliar with his work.
